title: Paced outbound calls to a courier quote API
name: Courier quote pacer

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code limits the rate of calls to the courier API? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: There is none. Only one timer is pending at a time (pump returns early while this.timer is set), each start sets nextSlotAt = now + minIntervalMs before running the task, and the next timer waits until that slot, so call starts are spaced at least 200 ms apart (at most 5/s). The queue is capped at 50, so memory and wait time are bounded and overflow fails fast. task() is invoked inside run(), so a synchronous throw from task would escape, but here the task is an async function, which turns throws into rejections forwarded via then(resolve, reject); the finally guarantees pumping continues.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Ten quote requests arrive at once on an idle service. Roughly when does the tenth courier API call start?
choices: After about 2 seconds, once the first call's timeout expires
choiceQuestions.explanation: The first call starts on a 0 ms timer, and each start schedules the next no earlier than 200 ms later, so call n starts about (n-1) x 200 ms: the tenth at about 1.8 s. Pacing is on start times, not completion, so it does not wait for the 2 s timeout; nothing allows simultaneous starts.

choiceQuestions.prompt: The courier API slows down so each call takes 1.5 seconds. What happens to concurrency?
choices: Calls still start every 200 ms, so up to about 8 can be in flight at once
Only one call is in flight at a time because the executor waits for each task
The executor stops starting calls until the slow ones finish
choiceQuestions.explanation: run() fires task() and returns without awaiting it, and pump() is called in finally right away, so the executor limits the start rate, not concurrency. With 1.5 s per call and a start every 200 ms, about 7-8 overlap. It does not serialize or pause, and the abort timeout is 2 s, not 200 ms.

choiceQuestions.prompt: During a spike, 80 quote requests arrive within a few milliseconds. What do callers see?
choices: All 80 get real quotes, just later
The first 50 are queued; the rest throw QueueFullError to the caller of quote()
Roughly the first 50 queue for real quotes; the remaining ~30 immediately get the fallback quote marked estimated
choiceQuestions.explanation: submit rejects with QueueFullError once 50 are waiting (one may already have been dequeued by the first timer, so the split is approximate). quote() catches QueueFullError and returns FALLBACK_QUOTE with estimated: true, so it is not rethrown. Queued requests are still served by the real API.
